incumbent.name: Samantha Hurst
incumbent.summary: Hurst was elected Perry County prosecutor in November 2022 {ipac_hurst}, defeating Democrat Jason R. Hoch {enr22g}, and is seeking a second term {enr26p}.
record: November 2022: Elected prosecutor with 3,581 votes to 2,670 for Democrat Jason R. Hoch {enr22g}.
July 2024 and October 2025: Hurst wrote bylined articles in the Perry County News explaining the facts and charges in individual criminal cases handled by her office {pcn_col1} {pcn_col2} {pcn_col3}.

July 21, 2026: Hurst and Judge Lucy Goffinet outlined the funding situation of the Perry County Drug Court for the county commissioners, who voted to help support the drug court while funding options remained unsettled {pcn_drug}.

race_context: Perry County forms Indiana's 70th Judicial Circuit {in_list}.
Incumbent Samantha Hurst was unopposed in the May 5, 2026 Republican primary with 567 votes {enr26p}. No Democrat appeared on the primary ballot {enr26p}.

Democrat Samuel Starks is on the general-election list with a filing date of June 9, 2026, after the primary {sos_gen_list}, consistent with a party filling a ballot vacancy; the method was not confirmed in sources reviewed.

The Perry County News hosted a candidate forum with Democratic and Republican candidates on Oct. 5, 2026 in Cannelton {pcn_forum}; coverage of what the prosecutor candidates said was not found in freely available text.
Starks was among the Perry County Democratic candidates recognized at the party's July 25, 2026 honors dinner in Tell City {pcn_dinner}.

candidates.summary: Incumbent Perry County prosecutor since January 2023, seeking a second term {ipac_hurst} {br_hurst}.
background: Perry County Prosecuting Attorney; elected November 2022 {ipac_hurst}.
Graduated from the University of Southern Indiana in 2014 and the Indiana University Maurer School of Law in 2017 {ipac_hurst}.
path_to_ballot: Filed for the Republican nomination Jan. 23, 2026 {sos_prim_list}; unopposed in the May 5, 2026 primary with 567 votes {enr26p}.
